---
title: "Weekly interactive chemistry demos"
---

Change one chemical condition, predict the result, and check the balance.
These five working study-week groupings follow the existing topic sequence;
they are a guide to using the demos rather than a formal timetable.

| Study week | Topics grouped for practice | Interactive question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Foundations and atmosphere, units 1–4 | [How do deposition, area, and water export affect load and concentration?](week1.qmd) |
| 2 | Aquatic composition, carbonate, and organic matter, units 5–7 | [Why do waters at the same initial pH respond differently to acid?](week2.qmd) |
| 3 | Metals, surfaces, redox, and treatment, units 8–11 | [How do free ligand and pH change metal binding and saturation?](week3.qmd) |
| 4 | Soils, waste, and organic contaminants, units 12–14 | [Where is parent compound accounted for during sorption and transformation?](week4.qmd) |
| 5 | Connected systems and synthesis, unit 15 | [How do neutralisation and water export affect the annual catchment budget?](week5.qmd) |

## How to use a demo

Make a prediction before moving a control. Use a reference-case button to set
all the inputs, then change one variable. Read both the visual result and the
calculated values; explain which quantity stayed conserved and which changed.
Reset restores the initial case. Keyboard arrow keys work when a slider is focused.

Each page includes a hand calculation, questions to try, and a static reference
that remains usable in print or without JavaScript. The demos run in the browser
with no login, data upload, or R installation. They use the same constructed
models as the course examples; adjustable inputs are not field measurements.
